text.title: Focus Groups: Structure, Moderation, and Analysis Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes first on the class of claim the finding must support — performance and demand questions leave the method entirely — then on room composition and the number of groups per segment, to decide between routing out, running with group-specific reporting, and the full moderated design.

decision-tree.root-question: What class of claim will this finding be used to make?

branch.when: task success, time on task, findability, or any statement of the form 'users can/cannot do X'

conclusion.verdict: skip; route to usability testing for task success, tree-testing-ux-research for findability, analytics for frequency — a group measures negotiated opinion, never performance

branch.when: willingness to pay, feature preference between options, or 'would you use this'

conclusion.verdict: skip or re-scope to past events; anything the group says here is stated intention and must never be cited as evidence of demand

branch.when: shared vocabulary, objections people raise in front of each other, or how an opinion shifts under group discussion
branch.question: Can the room be composed without a power or commercial relationship between attendees, and segmented on the variable expected to move the opinion?

branch.when: managers would sit with their direct reports, client with vendor, or teacher with students

conclusion.verdict: halt recruiting; re-screen to exclude co-attendance and split the sessions, or fall back to individual interviews

branch.when: the screener excludes co-attendance but mixes segments expected to disagree — current customers with churned, novices with experts

conclusion.verdict: re-screen into separate groups per segment before fielding; a mixed room converges on the loudest segment's frame

branch.when: the screener excludes co-attendance and segments cleanly
branch.question: How many groups can actually be run per segment?

branch.when: only one group per segment is affordable

conclusion.verdict: run it, but label every theme group-specific; no theme may be reported as a property of the segment on a single session

branch.when: the session would run over 120 minutes or seat more than 10 people to fit the guide

conclusion.verdict: cut the guide before fielding; 6-10 people, 90-120 minutes, roughly 8-10 main prompts, with the airtime arithmetic recorded in the artefact

branch.when: two or more groups per segment, sized within the airtime arithmetic

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; silent written answers before each open discussion, attribution log with per-participant turn share, sessions over the dominance thresholds flagged
